transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-07-10 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Evan Brooks (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Acme CTO), Priya Nair (Acme ML), Marcus Bell (Acme Infra), Liu Wen (Acme Security)

Summary: quick migration demo to show request/response parity and operational controls, plus next steps for a small POC.

[00:00] Maya (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros?
[00:08] Jordan: Jordan, CTO at Acme. we run a mix of OpenAI + Anthropic models in prod via Together for routing, trying to consolidate.
[00:15] Priya: Priya, ML engineer, i own the embed pipeline and some prompt infra.
[00:22] Marcus: Marcus - infra, concerned about VPC + egress and cost.
[00:28] Liu: Liu, security team, will ask about SOC2 and KMS.
[00:33] Maya: great, i'll pass to Samir to do a quick parity mapping and demo.
[00:40] Samir (SE): cool, so high level this is a migration walkthrough — we show how typical OpenAI/Together calls map to Redwood's endpoints, streaming, function calling, embeddings. I'll share my screen — apologies if the model names render weirdly, transcription may say 'Redwood brain' sometimes.
[01:05] Samir: first example, standard chat/completion. OpenAI style prompt/ messages -> Redwood has same message array shape but a different top-level param names, we accept both role/content and we map function calls to our 'tools' interface. code sample: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat -d '{"model":"rwd-large","messages":[..]}'
[01:40] Priya: how about streaming? we rely on chunked responses for our UI, any differences?
[01:47] Samir: streaming is identical in behavior, SSE style, you can consume tokens as they arrive. one small gotcha — Together had a slightly different delta object, but we provide a compatibility layer in the SDK that normalizes fields.
[02:10] Marcus: latency question — we're sensitive, 100ms p90 token delivery. can you hit those?
[02:18] Evan: depends on model + infra, but with Dedicated pools and pinning model variants we typically see 80-200ms per token for short responses on A100/RTX-class in our benchmarks. we also have routing policies to fall back to cheaper variants if capacity constrained.
[02:36] Jordan: and cost — switching vendors is about cost too. what levers do we have?
[02:41] Samir: batching, prefix/KV caching, quantization profiles. Optimize suggests batch sizes and quant configs per workload; that gives you 20-60% cost reduction depending on pattern.
[03:00] Priya: embeddings — our pipeline uses OpenAI embeddings (text-embedding-3-small). we need exact dimensional parity?
[03:08] Samir: Redwood provides multiple embedding models compatible with common dims, and we auto-handle encoding differences. we also have an embeddings migration guide with a small repro script — we'll include that.
[03:28] Liu: security — where does keys live? do you integrate with our KMS?
[03:33] Maya: yes, for Private/Dedicated we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM, and we can do VPC peering or private link. we have SOC2 Type II and can share the audit pack.
[03:50] Liu: any audit logs? need per-request logs with redaction options.
[03:54] Samir: yes, Console has token-level traces, per-route dashboards, and you can configure retention and redaction. we'll share the security pack which describes fields and retention controls.
[04:12] Jordan: about rollouts — we do canary traffic and A/B models across regions. can Redwood do weighted rollouts?
[04:18] Evan: yes, Console supports canary/A-B, automatic fallback on errors and capacity-based routing. you can pin commit hashes too.
[04:30] Priya: concretely, how does an OpenAI function call map? we use tools heavily.
[04:36] Samir: function calls map to Redwood's tools; same name, signature mapping. we also normalize type errors and return the original function response shape. example: if OpenAI returns 'function_call' with name/arguments, Redwood will emit the same fields. small naming differences in the SDKs but we include examples.
[05:05] Marcus: what about Together routing — we currently have a router that fans out to different models based on confidence. can Redwood integrate?
[05:13] Evan: yes, our smart routing layer supports policy rules by latency, cost, or model, and we can use external signals. there's also a lightweight adapter for Together routing logic.
[05:28] Jordan: do you provide request sampling for quality regression detection? we need to ensure outputs don't regress after migration.
[05:34] Samir: Optimize includes quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to prompt sets; you can upload canaries and have nightly evals.
[05:45] Priya: demo the Console — where do we see per-route metrics?
[05:50] Samir: switches to console view — here's per-route token breakdown, latency histograms, and a rollout panel. (screen notes: UI elements abbreviated).
[06:15] [Screen: Console showing routes, traces, and Optimize suggestions]
[06:40] Samir: here's a parity mapping doc tab — we annotate OpenAI/Together request fields -> Redwood equivalents and include sample cURLs and SDK snippets.
[06:58] Jordan: can you send that doc after the call?
[07:02] Maya: yes, we'll email it — action: Maya to send parity mapping + example cURLs.
[07:10] Priya: small nit — does Redwood preserve tokenization differences important for our embedding distances?
[07:16] Samir: tokenizer differences exist, but our embeddings migration guide includes a re-embedding strategy and sample thresholds; we can run a small compare on a sample set.
[07:30] Marcus: VPC details — we need private egress, no public internet.
[07:35] Maya: Private deployment supports VPC peering and on-prem options; we'll include network diagrams.
[07:42] Liu: SAML/SSO and RBAC?
[07:45] Evan: SSO via SAML/OIDC and fine-grained RBAC in Console; audit trails available.
[07:52] Jordan: regulatory — EU data residency?
[07:55] Maya: we have regions in EU and can support data residency on Dedicated or Private.
[08:05] [08:05] Priya: ok let's talk about a small POC — run 1 week of traffic or replay on 10%?
[08:12] Maya: recommended: replay a day's traffic for embeddings and 1-week for quality checks, or route 10% live traffic to Redwood for latency/cost numbers.
[08:22] Jordan: what's the lift to get a small POC? are there SDKs and quickstart?
[08:27] Samir: SDKs in Python/Node, quickstart with example mapping script. typically dev time is a few days to wire up; we'll provide runbook.
[08:36] Priya: any rate limits or quotas on Hosted?
[08:40] Maya: Hosted has quotas but Dedicated removes per-tenant noisy neighbor issues; Dedicated also gives you guaranteed throughput.
[08:48] Marcus: pricing for Dedicated — rough guess?
[08:51] Maya: we'll provide a ballpark in the pricing sheet — depends on GPUs, committed hours, and capacity. expect negotiation for 24/7 reserved pools.
[09:05] [09:05] Samir: quick tech deep dive — here's how we manage KV cache for long contexts; we maintain per-session KV to avoid recompute and we have eviction policies that you can tune.
[09:25] Priya: sounds good. what about quantization — we need to reduce cost for cheaper routes.
[09:30] Evan: Optimize suggests quant profiles; we support INT8/FP16 inference and can provide accuracy regressions for your prompt set.
[09:40] [Minor crosstalk, someone drops for a second]
[10:00] Jordan: ok, if we move forward what's the typical timeline to be able to serve production traffic?
[10:06] Maya: pilot can start within 2 weeks for a small POC (benchmarks + sample routing). Production depends on Dedicated procurement and networking — typically 6-10 weeks for end-to-end.
[10:20] Liu: procurement/legal will need data processing agreement and security addendum.
[10:25] Maya: we have standard templates and can loop in compliance.
[10:32] [10:32] Priya: i'd like Samir to run a perf harness on a subset — can we get sample loadshape?
[10:37] Samir: yes, please send sample request distribution — Jordan will share.
[10:42] Jordan: i'll export a sample and send it to the AE thread.
[10:48] Maya: recap: will send parity mapping doc, security pack, pricing sheet; Samir will run perf tests once we get sample traffic; Jordan team to provide request samples and SLOs; schedule POC scoping week of 7/20.
[11:05] Marcus: thanks all.
[11:10] Liu: thanks, will follow up with security questions.
[11:14] Maya: thanks everyone — i'll follow up via email with the docs and meeting notes.
[11:20] End of recording.
